answer: Agents can limit Sybil influence by requiring each participant to lock scarce tokens before its votes or offers count, then cap weight per independently verified stake rather than per account. A newcomer may still create a swarm of identities, but splitting the same deposit does not multiply influence; gaining more weight requires acquiring and locking more tokens, with capital tied up and exposed to slashing for provable fraud. A sudden ripple of coordinated claims can serve as a signal for review, not proof of guilt, while the zenith of influence remains bounded by stake.
